key_insight: PoreML provides a unified, physics-grounded pipeline for generating pore-scale multiphase-flow data and benchmarking ML models for prediction and rollout stability.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports more reliable surrogate modeling for porous-media applications such as CO2 storage, fuel cells, and packaging by standardizing data, training, and evaluation.
method: GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver for reproducible pore-scale simulation
3.3 TB dataset with 560 runs and 158,546 time steps across synthetic and micro-CT-derived geometries
Unified benchmark for one-step prediction, autoregressive rollout, and physical-consistency checks
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation against analytical solutions and experiments, plus evaluation of five model architectures on domain-shift challenges including larger domains and micro-CT-derived structures.
watch_item: Generalization may still be limited by the scarcity of real time-resolved 3D data and by distribution shifts between synthetic and micro-CT geometries.
paper_title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
